objectives.objective: AUTO: start with up to eight supported FUEL and score from a legal launch pose while the HUB is active
objectives.basis: The starting fold holds 14 or more FUEL by free volume behind the stowed intake (start-capacity premise), and the hopper-cycle-8-preload trial feeds eight from the hopper; the launch and flight cases carry a FUEL into the HUB opening from the 2.7 m pose that the re-run rehearsal credits in AUTO (delivery-pose premise). Delivering from 2.70 m costs no FUEL: slot 2 credits 124 in both the baseline and R3 series.

objectives.objective: Inactive shift: collect and hold the next allocated stock from the DEPOT, OUTPOST or a partner
objectives.basis: The acquire cases take a floor FUEL up the bumper face and the chute back plate and over its top along the acquisition trial's trace (inside the frame in 0.65 s); the hopper cases follow the entry trial to the stage, clamped under the feeder roller 1.44 s later. The hopper-collect-24-hold trial collects 24 through the chute: 24 in the hopper and 0 in the chute, none lost and none at the flywheel (hopper-capacity premise).

objectives.objective: Active shift: carry each FUEL from storage through one transfer into the HUB
objectives.basis: loaded-transit, the launch and flight cases carry the tracked FUEL from the stage into the HUB funnel along the launch and delivery trials' traces, to within the path tolerance each case declares. The feeder advances it only with the wheel in its ready band; it releases at 6.90 m/s and 61.6 degrees, and the delivery trials score from 6.725 to 7.100 m/s at the nominal drag and spin lift and at all four corners.

objectives.objective: Active shift: sustain 2.00 FUEL/s to score 24 with stock ready by second 5
objectives.basis: The batch trial launches 24 FUEL through the one flywheel at 4.0 FUEL/s, every release inside the scoring band, on a 12 V and on the 8.34 V weak-pack bus. The hopper cycle trial feeds 24 collected FUEL to the flywheel in 7.1-10.5 s over 16 arrival patterns (2.3-3.4 FUEL/s against 2.00), so the hopper, not the flywheel, sets the rate. The wheel spins up in 1.1 s (1.3 s on the weak pack) and is held at speed while FUEL is aboard. Bench tests are listed in verification-gates.json and in the risk register of missions.json.

objectives.objective: Fallback: score the available batch when supply or traffic consumes the window and return to collecting
objectives.basis: The cycle is piece-count independent: the hopper-cycle-8-preload trial feeds a part batch; the intake stays deployed in every scoring case; the re-run rehearsal keeps the depot loop.

objectives.objective: Traffic: remain in the own zone, keep possession through loaded driving and contact, and yield
objectives.basis: The hopper front is closed by the deployed intake's back plate to 425 mm and the walls rise to 715 mm. Every collect-hold-feed pattern carries its 24 FUEL through a 0.5 g stop, start and turn with none lost. Harder stops are tested on single patterns only: at 0.75 g 1 of 1 tested patterns keep and feed all 24; at 1 g 2 of 2 tested patterns keep and feed all 24. Loaded acceleration is limited to 0.5 g. The staged FUEL is clamped under a braked feeder roller: the hold trial keeps it 25.6 mm clear of the spinning wheel at 1.5 g with a 90 N push. Bench tests are listed in verification-gates.json and in the risk register of missions.json.

objectives.objective: Neutral collector alternative with two field crossings
objectives.basis: The coordinator selected the own-zone role. R3 keeps a BUMP crossing option (bump-crossing premise, 8.7 mm least clearance) with the intake retracted.

objectives.objective: End game: Level 1 low-rung hang when its expected 10 points exceed the remaining FUEL service
objectives.basis: With the hopper empty the hooks swing forward, the intake stows between them, the robot closes on the TOWER, seats (2 mm required contact) and lifts 70 mm; the 714 mm frame gives 23.9 mm of bumper overlap with each upright (hang-bumper-overlap premise); the hang physics trial at 70.3 kg holds 37.5 mm with the brake and fails without it; its cable load peaks at 1043 N in the lift and settles at 690 N. Bench tests are listed in verification-gates.json and in the risk register of missions.json.

objectives.objective: AUTO Level 1 TOWER (15 points, two-robot cap)
objectives.basis: The strategy keeps the eight-FUEL AUTO objective; no joined AUTO climb evidence is sought in this layout.

objectives.basis: Alliance routing decision owned by the field rehearsal, independent of the robot layout.

floor belt main.rationale: Flat belts in the channel at 1.2 m/s, running to the front rail so a FUEL at the front of the floor stands on a driven surface. They stop while both lanes are staged and held, and reverse for 0.3 s in an unjam cycle. At 0.6 and 0.3 m/s the hopper cycle trial feeds all 24 in 15.8 and 14.3 s, against 7.6 s at this speed.
floor belt main.material: Belt envelope; flat belt and rollers
floor belt main.name: Floor belt main

floor belt front.purpose: Carry the floor layer of FUEL aft to the feeder rollers.
floor belt front.rationale: Flat belts in the channel at 1.2 m/s, running to the front rail so a FUEL at the front of the floor stands on a driven surface. They stop while both lanes are staged and held, and reverse for 0.3 s in an unjam cycle. At 0.6 and 0.3 m/s the hopper cycle trial feeds all 24 in 15.8 and 14.3 s, against 7.6 s at this speed.
floor belt front.material: Belt envelope; flat belt and rollers
floor belt front.name: Floor belt front

feeder roller left.purpose: Hold a staged FUEL clear of the spinning flywheel, and feed it on command.
feeder roller left.rationale: One compliant 2 in roller per lane, 14 mm into the FUEL over the fixed lane deck. Braked, it is the hold-back: the hold trial keeps the FUEL 25.6 mm clear of the wheel at 1.5 g with a 90 N push and fails at 120 N. Turning, it meters: the lanes feed the one flywheel in turn, each feed given only with the wheel in its ready band. The two rollers meet at the centre line so a FUEL between the lanes is still under a roller.
feeder roller left.material: 2 in compliant roller on a 12 mm shaft
feeder roller left.name: Feeder roller left

feeder roller right.purpose: Hold a staged FUEL clear of the spinning flywheel, and feed it on command.
feeder roller right.rationale: One compliant 2 in roller per lane, 14 mm into the FUEL over the fixed lane deck. Braked, it is the hold-back: the hold trial keeps the FUEL 25.6 mm clear of the wheel at 1.5 g with a 90 N push and fails at 120 N. Turning, it meters: the lanes feed the one flywheel in turn, each feed given only with the wheel in its ready band. The two rollers meet at the centre line so a FUEL between the lanes is still under a roller.
feeder roller right.material: 2 in compliant roller on a 12 mm shaft
feeder roller right.name: Feeder roller right

feeder motor left.purpose: Turn and brake one feeder roller.
feeder motor left.rationale: A small planetary gearmotor with a brake outboard of the channel wall, under the shelf on the left and in the pocket on the right. Unmounted allowance: the 12 mm shaft through the channel wall and the bearing block that carries it are not drawn, so the motor appears to float.
feeder motor left.name: Feeder motor left (unmounted allowance)

feeder motor right.purpose: Turn and brake one feeder roller.
feeder motor right.rationale: A small planetary gearmotor with a brake outboard of the channel wall, under the shelf on the left and in the pocket on the right. Unmounted allowance: the 12 mm shaft through the channel wall and the bearing block that carries it are not drawn, so the motor appears to float.
feeder motor right.name: Feeder motor right (unmounted allowance)

flywheel.purpose: Accelerate each FUEL against the hood.
flywheel.rationale: A 4 in floor-fed flywheel at a 13.6 m/s setpoint, held at speed whenever FUEL is aboard. The wheel-to-hood gap is the FUEL diameter less 12 mm: the launch trial releases at 6.90 m/s. It is a free body in the trial: one shot takes 17 J and drops it 1.9%.
flywheel.name: Flywheel

flywheel inertia ring.purpose: Store the energy of a shot so the wheel speed falls little.
flywheel inertia ring.rationale: One steel ring (0.97 kg) outboard of the right side plate brings the wheel to 0.0076 kg m2 for 2.56 kg. The batch trial holds the scoring band with it on the weak-pack bus; the bare roller holds it there only at the full 40 A stator limit.
flywheel inertia ring.material: Steel ring on an aluminum web; drawn as its disc envelope
flywheel inertia ring.name: Flywheel inertia ring

hood.purpose: Guide the FUEL around the flywheel and release it at about 62 degrees elevation.
hood.rationale: Concentric with the wheel and tangent to the lane deck. It ends at -149.5 degrees about the wheel axis, where the launch trial releases the FUEL at 61.6 degrees; the end stays inside the rear perimeter, so the shooter never extends a second side.
hood.name: Hood

shooter side plate left.purpose: Carry the flywheel bearings and hood.
shooter side plate left.rationale: Plates stop 4 mm short of the rear modules and bound the two lanes behind the rear wall.
shooter side plate left.name: Shooter side plate left

shooter side plate right.purpose: Carry the flywheel bearings and hood.
shooter side plate right.rationale: Plates stop 4 mm short of the rear modules and bound the two lanes behind the rear wall.
shooter side plate right.name: Shooter side plate right

flywheel motor left.purpose: Drive the flywheel from both ends and hold its speed.
flywheel motor left.rationale: Direct drive, 40 A stator and 30 A supply limit each. Outboard of each side plate, clear of the battery, the ring and the rear modules.
flywheel motor left.name: Flywheel motor left

flywheel motor right.purpose: Drive the flywheel from both ends and hold its speed.
flywheel motor right.rationale: Direct drive, 40 A stator and 30 A supply limit each. Outboard of each side plate, clear of the battery, the ring and the rear modules.
flywheel motor right.name: Flywheel motor right

battery.rationale: Standing on its end under the left shelf, between two cleats and under a strap; it lifts straight out once the shelf panel and strap are off.
battery.name: Battery

battery retention cleat aft.purpose: Stop the battery sliding aft and carry its end load into the floor pan.
battery retention cleat aft.rationale: Paired with the fore cleat so the battery is captured in X.
battery retention cleat aft.name: Battery retention cleat aft

battery retention cleat fore.rationale: Paired with the aft cleat so the battery is captured in X while it still lifts straight out for service.
battery retention cleat fore.name: Battery retention cleat fore

battery strap.purpose: Hold the battery down on the floor pan.
battery strap.rationale: The earlier issue had no hold-down. The strap runs over the battery top between the cleats, under the shelf panel.
battery strap.name: Battery strap

electronics panel.purpose: Hold power distribution, controller, radio, breaker and 17 motor controllers.
electronics panel.rationale: Under the right shelf, beside the battery and under the right slide rail: outside the FUEL space and reachable from above or from the side. The panel under the shelf stands on the floor pan.
electronics panel.name: Electronics panel

electronics panel left.purpose: Hold power distribution, controller, radio, breaker and 17 motor controllers.
electronics panel left.rationale: Under the right shelf, beside the battery and under the right slide rail: outside the FUEL space and reachable from above or from the side. The panel under the shelf stands on the floor pan.
electronics panel left.name: Electronics panel left

electronics bay right.purpose: Hold power distribution, controller, radio, breaker and 17 motor controllers.
electronics bay right.rationale: Under the right shelf, beside the battery and under the right slide rail: outside the FUEL space and reachable from above or from the side. The panel under the shelf stands on the floor pan.
electronics bay right.name: Electronics bay right

entry sensor.purpose: Observe each FUEL passing the top of the chute, and that the chute is clear before the intake stows.
entry sensor.rationale: The strategy requires per-piece intake crossings on the match timebase.
entry sensor.name: Entry sensor

stage sensor left.purpose: Observe the FUEL staged under each feeder roller.
stage sensor left.rationale: One beam per lane: a FUEL on the centre line breaks both, and both rollers then hold or feed it together. Separates retained identity from release for the counting requirement.
stage sensor left.name: Stage sensor left

stage sensor right.purpose: Observe the FUEL staged under each feeder roller.
stage sensor right.rationale: One beam per lane: a FUEL on the centre line breaks both, and both rollers then hold or feed it together. Separates retained identity from release for the counting requirement.
stage sensor right.name: Stage sensor right

climber tube right.rationale: Front corners above the modules give a straight load path into the frame for the hang.

climber winch.purpose: Retract both inner tubes by cable to lift the robot.
climber winch.rationale: Under the left slide rail, outboard of the carriage plate. In the hang trial at 70.3 kg its cable load peaks at 1043 N during the lift, and the brake must hold 690 N with power removed.
climber winch.name: Climber winch

climber inner tube left.purpose: Telescope inside the outer tube to seat the hook and lift the robot 70 mm.
climber inner tube left.rationale: A round tube lets the hook swing on top without the tube rotating in its guide; the swing actuator sits inside it.
climber inner tube left.name: Climber inner tube left

climber inner tube right.purpose: Telescope inside the outer tube to seat the hook and lift the robot 70 mm.
climber inner tube right.rationale: A round tube lets the hook swing on top without the tube rotating in its guide; the swing actuator sits inside it.
climber inner tube right.name: Climber inner tube right

climber hook left.purpose: Swing forward, pass over the low rung, seat and lift the robot 70 mm.
climber hook left.rationale: Stowed inside the perimeter for R106. They swing while the intake is still deployed below them; the intake then stows between them.
climber hook left.name: Climber hook left

climber hook right.purpose: Swing forward, pass over the low rung, seat and lift the robot 70 mm.
climber hook right.rationale: Stowed inside the perimeter for R106. They swing while the intake is still deployed below them; the intake then stows between them.
climber hook right.name: Climber hook right

intake belt module.purpose: Draw a floor FUEL under its bottom pulley and lift it up the bumper face and the back plate.
intake belt module.rationale: Drawn at the acquisition trial's setting: the back run stands 20 mm inside one FUEL diameter from the bumper face and the back plate, and the bottom pulley 20 mm into a floor FUEL. The trial captures at 15 mm and fails at 10 mm, so the squeeze is a layout dimension. It stays inside the 304.8 mm reach. Unmounted allowance: its tie to the carriage plates is not drawn, so it appears to float 6 mm inside them. The hopper cheek stands between it and the plate while the intake is stowed, so the tie has to pass over or ahead of the cheek (risk carriage-cross-ties).
intake belt module.name: Intake belt module

intake top roller.purpose: Throw the lifted FUEL aft over the top of the back plate.
intake top roller.rationale: Lowered 20 mm into the path of the FUEL at the top of the climb and turning at 2 times the belt speed; the FUEL enters the hopper at 1.9 m/s, 552 mm up, above the stored FUEL. Unmounted allowance: its tie to the carriage plates is not drawn, so it appears to float above and inside them. The hopper cheek stands between it and the plate while the intake is stowed, so the tie has to pass over or ahead of the cheek (risk carriage-cross-ties).
intake top roller.material: 2 in compliant wheels on hex shaft
intake top roller.name: Intake top roller

intake back plate.purpose: Back the belt above the bumper, and close the front of the hopper while the intake is deployed.
intake back plate.rationale: It continues the bumper face plane up to 425 mm, so a FUEL enters the hopper from above the heap: thrown in low through an open throat, the collect trial stalls with FUEL backing out. Its hopper-side face leans forward from a 45 mm foot, so a FUEL touching it stands over the driven belt. In an unjam cycle the slide nudges it 40 mm into the FUEL at the front. Unmounted allowance: its tie to the carriage plates is not drawn, so it appears to float 6 mm inside them. The hopper cheek stands between it and the plate while the intake is stowed, so the tie has to pass over or ahead of the cheek (risk carriage-cross-ties).
intake back plate.material: Folded 1 mm aluminum wedge with a friction face; drawn solid
intake back plate.name: Intake back plate

intake carriage plate left.purpose: Join the belt module, top roller and back plate to the slide, and close the sides of the chute.
intake carriage plate left.rationale: Plates at 250-260 mm run outboard of the hopper cheeks and inboard of the slide rails, and pass over the front module motors as the carriage deploys. Unmounted allowance: only the fixed stage of the two-stage slide is drawn, so a deployed plate appears to float ahead of its rail. The moving stage and the cross-ties to the belt module, top roller and back plate are not drawn (risk carriage-cross-ties).
intake carriage plate left.name: Intake carriage plate left

intake carriage plate right.purpose: Join the belt module, top roller and back plate to the slide, and close the sides of the chute.

presentation.title: Floor-fed hood shooter with a chute intake and a two-lane hopper
presentation.focus: FUEL tracked: The mission cases follow this FUEL from the carpet into the HUB.
notes: What it is: the whole-robot preliminary blockout of the Chute-fed hood shooter (floor-fed hooded-flywheel shooter with a chute intake and a two-lane hopper on a 680 x 714 mm four-module swerve base). Solids are planning envelopes and simplified material blocks, not a Fusion robot.

Simplified: swerve modules are body, motor and azimuth envelopes; electronics are panel blocks; belts and rollers are rigid outlines; the back plate is drawn solid. The intake belt, top roller, back plate, feeder roller, flywheel and hood are drawn at the squeeze the physics trials use (dimensions.py), so the tracked FUEL overlaps them by the trial's indentation; each such pair is an intended contact in its case, listed in contacts.json.

Field: the HUB and TOWER are parts of FIRST's official field model (cad/field/official/), placed at the shot pose in their official positions relative to each other. Fasteners, tags, lights and the fuel counter are left out. The physics trials ran earlier against dimensioned surfaces, not these parts.

Tracked FUEL motion: its 9 checked cases are coarse strokes fitted to the solved acquire, entry, launch and deliver trials in field-trials.json, each within the path tolerance its case declares (largest fit error 39.8 mm). Each stroke is uniform in its own parameter, so playback timing inside a case is not the trial's. The replays after the checked cases play the recorded trials themselves.

Solved in the trials: the FUEL against every surface; the intake belt speed under its motor and current limits; the flywheel speed under the FUEL's load and its motors. Imposed: robot approach speed (0.5 m/s), floor belt speed (1.2 m/s) and feeder roller speeds (0.6 and 1.2 m/s).

Replays: one FUEL from the carpet into the HUB, the 24-FUEL collect, hold and feed cycle, the hold-back, the 24-shot batch and the hang are recorded physics trials in field-trials.json. The hopper cycle fed all 24 in 7.1-10.5 s over 16 arrival patterns.

Prescribed, not simulated, in the checked cases: the intake slide, the field moving in the robot frame (TOWER approach), the hook swing and the climb strokes: battery-cover-remove, battery-withdraw, climb-reach, climb-seat, intake-deploy, intake-stow, loaded-transit, park-lower, shooter-withdraw, tower-forward, tower-lateral.
Contact stiffness, damping, friction and rolling resistance are estimates, not measurements, and no FUEL force-deflection curve is available. Motor figures are a published brushless curve.

Sources and cutoff: FRC REBUILT kickoff manual V0 with Team Update 00, cutoff 2026-01-10 23:59:59 America/New_York (construction-rules.json); official field STEP stamped 2026-01-07 (cad/field/official/official-field.json).
Risks closed by design and bench tests still to run: see openItems.

Closed by design (flywheel-droop): The flywheel slows under each shot and through a batch, and the release leaves the scoring band. Flywheel a free 0.0076 kg m2 body (roller plus one inertia ring, 2.56 kg) under two motors and a speed loop, fed only inside a 1% ready band: one shot takes 17 J and drops the wheel 1.9%; 24 FUEL at 4 FUEL/s release at 6.88-6.92 m/s on a 12 V bus and 6.83-6.88 m/s on the 8.34 V weak-pack bus, inside the 6.725-7.100 m/s band (batch trials).

Closed by design (hold-back): A staged FUEL is pushed into the spinning flywheel with no feed commanded. One braked feeder roller per lane over a fixed lane deck, 14 mm squeeze, floor belt ending ahead of the staged FUEL and stopped while both lanes are staged: the hold trial keeps the FUEL 25.6 mm clear under a 90 N push at 1.5 g and fails at 120 N. In the 16 collect-hold-feed patterns the push on a staged FUEL peaks at 138 N (20 ms mean), above the steady push the hold trial passes, as FUEL land on the heap, and no pattern feeds uncommanded; the bench tests hold-back-force and uncommanded-feed-bench measure the margin.

Closed by design (intake-power): The intake belt cannot hold its speed under the acquisition load at its current limit. Belt driven in the trial by one motor at 2:1 with a 30 A supply limit: three FUEL abreast on a 9 V bus dip it to 2.13 m/s and are captured; the trial captures down to 2.5 m/s and fails at 2 m/s.

Closed by design (batch-collection): A batch of 24 cannot be collected: thrown in low through an open throat, the hopper stalls with FUEL backing out into the intake. The intake is a chute that lifts each FUEL up its own back plate to 425 mm and throws it in over the top; the back plate closes the hopper front. Collect trial: 24 in the hopper and 0 in the chute of 24; collecting 27 leaves more than four in the chute (bracket). The earlier issue's low entry fails the same trial (control).

Closed by design (batch-feed): The collected heap bridges or strands FUEL and the feed falls below 2.00 FUEL/s. Two-lane channel with the belt running to the front rail, sloped shelves, feeder rollers standing in the hopper and meeting at the centre line, one stage beam per lane, a belt reversal and a 40 mm carriage nudge in the unjam cycle: 16 of 16 collect-hold-feed patterns feed all 24 in 7.1-10.5 s (2.3-3.4 FUEL/s).

Closed by design (hang-with-fuel): The intake cannot stow with FUEL in the front of the hopper, and deployed it stands under the rung. The hang sequence swings the hooks forward first, then stows the empty intake between them, then closes on the TOWER (cases climb-reach, intake-stow, tower-forward, checked). The stow is commanded only with the chute and both stage beams clear; with FUEL aboard the robot keeps shooting and does not hang, which is the strategy's own rule.

Closed by design (battery-strap): The battery has no hold-down. A strap over the battery top between the two cleats is drawn and mounted, and the shelf panel above it covers it; the service cases remove the panel and strap, then lift the battery (checked).

Closed by design (unregistered-joints): Members carried no registered joint to the frame. Each separately mounted member has its own mount entry: both feeder rollers and motors, both carriage plates, both inner tubes, both hooks, both climber tubes, the winch, the side walls, liners, rear wall, shelf panel and strap.

Bench test (shot-calibration): The model's wheel-to-FUEL speed transfer, drag and spin lift are estimates, so the setpoint that centres the release in the band is not known. The delivery trial also scored against a dimensioned opening, not the official HUB: the official opening is larger along the shot line, its funnel walls slope inward below the rim and a net stands behind it, and the trial's nominal shot arrives 384 mm beyond the HUB centre, where the net's lower edge is. Measure: FUEL scored of 20 launched from the 2.7 m pose, with every measured release speed of a 24 FUEL batch inside the band found on the bench; pass 19, fail 18 FUEL.

Bench test (hold-back-force): The hold rests on foam friction and stiffness that are estimates (0.9 and 0.6, 15 kN/m). Measure: Steady push on a staged FUEL that the braked feeder holds without the FUEL reaching the wheel; pass 90, fail 60 N.

Bench test (acquisition-pinch): Capture depends on the belt squeeze and on cover and back plate friction, which are estimates. Measure: Floor FUEL thrown over the back plate within 1.2 s, of 20, at 17.5, 20 and 25 mm squeeze with the belt at or above 2.5 m/s; pass 20, fail 19 FUEL.

Bench test (feed-rate-bench): Heap behaviour varies from run to run and rests on FUEL-to-FUEL and wall friction estimates; the slowest pattern feeds 24 in 10.5 s against 12 s. Measure: FUEL fed to the flywheel within 12 s of the first feed command, 24 collected through the chute, in each of 5 runs; pass 22, fail 21 FUEL.

Bench test (loaded-driving): A hard stop can throw FUEL forward over the chute, which is open above the top roller. Harder stops are tested on single patterns only: at 0.75 g 1 of 1 tested patterns keep and feed all 24; at 1 g 2 of 2 tested patterns keep and feed all 24. Measure: FUEL leaving the robot across ten stops from 3 m/s and five turns at the loaded acceleration limit of 0.5 g with 24 aboard; pass 0, fail 1 FUEL.
Bench test (uncommanded-feed-bench): A FUEL reaches the flywheel while collecting or driving. Measure: Uncommanded feeds in 20 collect-and-drive cycles of 24 FUEL; pass 0, fail 1 feeds.

Bench test (mass-reserve): The inspection weight estimate tops out 2.20 kg under the 52.16 kg limit. Measure: Weighed inspection weight of the robot without bumpers and battery; pass 52.16, fail 52.17 kg.

Bench test (hang-squaring): The robot hangs yawed or offset and a bumper misses an upright. The hang trial used a dimensioned TOWER BASE 8 mm tall; the official base plate and its brackets are checked for clearance in the climb cases but are not in the trial. Measure: Least clearance to the carpet and TOWER BASE through the 3 s hold, at 70.3 kg, seated at 0 and at 20 mm lateral offset each way; pass 5, fail 0 mm.

Bench test (bump-clearance): The front bumper corner clears the BUMP crest by 8.7 mm in the static screen, which uses a sharp 15 degree profile. The official BUMP crest is rounded and stands 3.7 mm fuller 20 mm either side of the line (cad/field/official/README.md), which is not in the screen. Measure: Least clearance of any part other than wheels and bumpers over the BUMP in ten crossings each way, intake retracted; pass 5, fail 0 mm.

Bench test (carriage-cross-ties): The intake's belt module, top roller and back plate stand inside the hopper cheeks and its carriage plates outside them. The ties between them and the moving slide stage are not drawn, so the layout does not show that they clear the cheeks and the bay walls through the slide travel. Measure: Least clearance from the carriage cross-ties and the moving slide stage to the hopper cheeks and bay walls over the full slide travel, on the first assembled carriage; pass 3, fail 1 mm.

Bench test (service-reserve): The battery, shelf panel and shooter withdrawals are checked for interference only, with no clearance reserve, because the layout check cannot hold a reserve in an extraction case beside official field parts that touch each other. Measure: Least clearance while lifting out the shelf panel, the battery and the shooter module on the first assembled robot; pass 3, fail 1 mm.

Bench test (weak-battery-margin): The loaded-transit duty leaves the smallest voltage margin on a weak battery. Measure: Minimum bus voltage through a loaded transit with the flywheel spinning up, on a battery at 0.026 ohm; pass 7.5, fail 7.0 V.

Bench test (carriage-nudge): The unjam cycle's carriage nudge has to push the back plate into the FUEL at the hopper front. In the recorded trials the pattern run without the nudge also feeds all 24, so the trials do not show the nudge is needed. Measure: Arches at the hopper front cleared by one 40 mm nudge, of 10 set by hand with 24 FUEL aboard; pass 10, fail 9 arches.

Bench test (bump-crossing-dynamic): Driving over the BUMP at speed with stored FUEL is not evaluated. Measure: FUEL leaving the robot in ten BUMP crossings each way at 1.5 m/s with 24 aboard and the intake retracted; pass 0, fail 1 FUEL.

Bench test (loaded-robot-contact): Robot-to-robot contact while carrying FUEL is not evaluated. Measure: FUEL leaving the robot in five 1 m/s bumper-to-bumper contacts on each side with 24 aboard; pass 1, fail 2 FUEL.
The loaded acceleration limit of 0.5 g is not in the field rehearsal: its cycle times were credited without it and are not re-run here.
The feeder shafts through the channel walls, the right climber cable across the front rail and the hood's thickness are not drawn.
The stowed carriage stands in the front half of the hopper, so the intake cannot stow while FUEL is forward of the stage; the hang is taken with the hopper empty.
